lines.text: What's the two thousand twenty-sixth whole number that is NOT a perfect square?
lines.caption: What's the two thousand twenty-sixth whole number that is NOT a perfect square?

lines.text: Counting them one by one would take all day. But there's a pattern hiding in the gaps.
lines.caption: Counting them one by one would take all day. But there's a pattern hiding in the gaps.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's knock out the squares and count what's left.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's knock out the squares and count what's left.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: List the positive whole numbers that are not perfect squares, in order.
lines.caption: List the positive whole numbers that are not perfect squares, in order.

lines.text: The list goes two, three, five, six, seven, eight, ten, and so on.
lines.caption: The list goes two, three, five, six, seven, eight, ten, and so on.

lines.text: What is the two thousand twenty-sixth number in the list?
lines.caption: What is the two thousand twenty-sixth number in the list?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what's going on? Start with the counting numbers, and knock out every perfect square.
lines.caption: So what's going on? Start with the counting numbers, and knock out every perfect square.

lines.text: One, four, nine and sixteen are gone. Every number left gets a spot in line.
lines.caption: One, four, nine and sixteen are gone. Every number left gets a spot in line.

lines.text: Two is in spot one, three is in spot two, and five is in spot three.
lines.caption: Two is in spot one, three is in spot two, and five is in spot three.

lines.text: We want the number in spot two thousand twenty-six. The spot and the number are NOT the same!
lines.caption: We want the number in spot two thousand twenty-six. The spot and the number are NOT the same!

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Strategy one: count the gaps between the squares.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Strategy one: count the gaps between the squares.

lines.text: Between one and four, two numbers survive. Between four and nine, four survive.
lines.caption: Between one and four, two numbers survive. Between four and nine, four survive.

lines.text: Between nine and sixteen, six survive. The gaps go two, four, six, eight, growing by two.
lines.caption: Between nine and sixteen, six survive. The gaps go two, four, six, eight, growing by two.

lines.text: After k squared, the gap holds two k numbers. The next square is k squared plus two k plus one.
lines.caption: After k squared, the gap holds two k numbers. The next square is k squared plus two k plus one.

lines.text: Now add up the gaps. Two, then six, then twelve, then twenty.
lines.caption: Now add up the gaps. Two, then six, then twelve, then twenty.

lines.text: That's one times two, two times three, three times four, four times five. See the pattern?
lines.caption: That's one times two, two times three, three times four, four times five. See the pattern?

lines.text: Try forty-four gaps: forty-four times forty-five is one thousand nine hundred eighty. Just under!
lines.caption: Try forty-four gaps: forty-four times forty-five is one thousand nine hundred eighty. Just under!

lines.text: So k gaps hold k times k plus one numbers.
lines.caption: So k gaps hold k times k plus one numbers.

lines.text: Forty-five gaps would be forty-five times forty-six, two thousand seventy. Too many!
lines.caption: Forty-five gaps would be forty-five times forty-six, two thousand seventy. Too many!

lines.text: Those are all the survivors below forty-five squared, which is two thousand twenty-five.
lines.caption: Those are all the survivors below forty-five squared, which is two thousand twenty-five.

lines.text: Hop over it. Then two thousand twenty-six takes spot one thousand nine hundred eighty-one.
lines.caption: Hop over it. Then two thousand twenty-six takes spot one thousand nine hundred eighty-one.

lines.text: We want spot two thousand twenty-six. That's forty-six more than spot one thousand nine hundred eighty.
lines.caption: We want spot two thousand twenty-six. That's forty-six more than spot one thousand nine hundred eighty.

lines.text: So count forty-six numbers past two thousand twenty-five.
lines.caption: So count forty-six numbers past two thousand twenty-five.

lines.text: Two thousand twenty-five plus forty-six is <short pause> two thousand seventy-one! Choice C.
lines.caption: Two thousand twenty-five plus forty-six is two thousand seventy-one! Choice C.

lines.text: The gap after forty-five squared holds ninety numbers, so we never hit another square.
lines.caption: The gap after forty-five squared holds ninety numbers, so we never hit another square.

lines.text: Here's a second way. Think about what the knocked-out squares do.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. Think about what the knocked-out squares do.

lines.text: Each square below the answer pushes it one spot along. So add HOW MANY squares there are.
lines.caption: Each square below the answer pushes it one spot along. So add HOW MANY squares there are.

lines.text: First guess: two thousand twenty-six, plus the squares up to it.
lines.caption: First guess: two thousand twenty-six, plus the squares up to it.

lines.text: Forty-five squared is two thousand twenty-five. So we skip forty-five perfect squares.
lines.caption: Forty-five squared is two thousand twenty-five. So we skip forty-five perfect squares.

lines.text: Two thousand twenty-six plus forty-five is two thousand seventy-one.
lines.caption: Two thousand twenty-six plus forty-five is two thousand seventy-one.

lines.text: Now check! Did we jump over a new square on the way?
lines.caption: Now check! Did we jump over a new square on the way?

lines.text: The next square is forty-six squared, two thousand one hundred sixteen. We're safe!
lines.caption: The next square is forty-six squared, two thousand one hundred sixteen. We're safe!

lines.text: Here's a shortcut for test day. Find the perfect square nearest to the spot number, and add its root.
lines.caption: Here's a shortcut for test day. Find the perfect square nearest to the spot number, and add its root.

lines.text: The nearest square to two thousand twenty-six is forty-five squared. Add forty-five. Same answer!
lines.caption: The nearest square to two thousand twenty-six is forty-five squared. Add forty-five. Same answer!

lines.text: Numbers between k squared and the next square have spots near k squared. And k squares came before.
lines.caption: Numbers between k squared and the next square have spots near k squared. And k squares came before.

lines.text: When would you pick this one? When the clock is ticking. Just remember to check.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? When the clock is ticking. Just remember to check.

lines.text: Now the traps. Here's a handy test: the spot is the number, minus how many squares come before it.
lines.caption: Now the traps. Here's a handy test: the spot is the number, minus how many squares come before it.

lines.text: Choice A, two thousand sixty-nine, minus forty-five, lands in spot two thousand twenty-four. Too early.
lines.caption: Choice A, two thousand sixty-nine, minus forty-five, lands in spot two thousand twenty-four. Too early.

lines.text: B, two thousand seventy, is what you'd get if you forgot that one is a perfect square too.
lines.caption: B, two thousand seventy, is what you'd get if you forgot that one is a perfect square too.

lines.text: Test it: take away forty-five, and you land in spot two thousand twenty-five. Too early.
lines.caption: Test it: take away forty-five, and you land in spot two thousand twenty-five. Too early.

lines.text: D, two thousand seventy-two, is what you'd get by adding forty-six instead of forty-five.
lines.caption: D, two thousand seventy-two, is what you'd get by adding forty-six instead of forty-five.

lines.text: Test it: take away forty-five, and you land in spot two thousand twenty-seven. Too late.
lines.caption: Test it: take away forty-five, and you land in spot two thousand twenty-seven. Too late.

lines.text: E, two thousand one hundred sixteen, is forty-six squared. It isn't even in the list!
lines.caption: E, two thousand one hundred sixteen, is forty-six squared. It isn't even in the list!

lines.text: So here's a great habit. After you add the squares, check that you didn't jump over a new one.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. After you add the squares, check that you didn't jump over a new one.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same list, a new spot.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same list, a new spot.

lines.text: What is the one thousandth number in the list?
lines.caption: What is the one thousandth number in the list?

lines.text: You can use either way. And don't forget to check!
lines.caption: You can use either way. And don't forget to check!

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Thirty-one squared is nine hundred sixty-one. That's thirty-one perfect squares below one thousand.
lines.caption: Thirty-one squared is nine hundred sixty-one. That's thirty-one perfect squares below one thousand.

lines.text: First guess: one thousand plus thirty-one, which is one thousand thirty-one.
lines.caption: First guess: one thousand plus thirty-one, which is one thousand thirty-one.

lines.text: Now check. Thirty-two squared is one thousand twenty-four. We jumped right over it!
lines.caption: Now check. Thirty-two squared is one thousand twenty-four. We jumped right over it!

lines.text: So push one more spot. The answer is <short pause> one thousand thirty-two!
lines.caption: So push one more spot. The answer is one thousand thirty-two!

lines.text: Check again: thirty-three squared is one thousand eighty-nine, safely past it.
lines.caption: Check again: thirty-three squared is one thousand eighty-nine, safely past it.

lines.text: The shortcut agrees: the nearest square to one thousand is thirty-two squared. Add thirty-two.
lines.caption: The shortcut agrees: the nearest square to one thousand is thirty-two squared. Add thirty-two.

lines.text: Big idea: the answer is its spot, plus HOW MANY squares sit below it. Then check for one more!
lines.caption: Big idea: the answer is its spot, plus HOW MANY squares sit below it. Then check for one more!

lines.text: Or use the shortcut: add the root of the perfect square nearest to the spot number.
lines.caption: Or use the shortcut: add the root of the perfect square nearest to the spot number.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
